documents: Xu, Stovas & Huang (2023) Umbilic points of slowness surface in elastic orthorhombic media, Geophysical Prospecting 71:385-403 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: This paper aims to investigate the influence of the existence of the umbilic points on the slowness surface

steps.action: Pose the question of where umbilic points sit on ORT slowness surfaces and how they affect kinematic characteristics such as traveltime.
steps.quote: This paper aims to investigate the influence of the existence of the umbilic points on the slowness surface

steps.action: Take from earlier work the expectation that traveltime near umbilic points behaves as a shifted hyperbola, and the equal-principal-curvature criterion for umbilics.
steps.quote: In the vicinity of umbilic points, traveltime behaves like a shifted (both in time and offset) hyperbola (Stovas & Fomel, 2012).

steps.action: Build the procedure: the condition H^2 - K = 0 from Gaussian and mean curvatures of the slowness surface (eqs 1-8), the centre of curvature and radius (eqs 9-10), and the shifted-hyperbola slowness, group velocity and traveltime near the umbilic (eqs 11-16).
steps.quote: The equal principal curvature condition can provide the position of the umbilic points

steps.action: Derive the characteristic equations and vertical slownesses for the decoupled P wave and the coupled S waves in the elliptical ORT model (eqs 17-23).
steps.quote: To derive analytical formulas for the positions of umbilic points, we select the elliptical orthorhombic (ORT) model

steps.action: Set seven synthetic elliptical ORT models (stiffnesses in Table 1, Thomsen-type parameters in Table 2) with fixed vertical P and S velocities.
steps.quote: We introduce seven elliptical ORT models with the normalized stiffness coefficients shown in Table 1.

steps.action: Contour the umbilic condition function for elliptical models 1 and 5 and locate its zeros on the [X,Z] or [Y,Z] planes for the P, S1 and S2 waves (Figure 2).
steps.quote: First, we show the counterplot for the condition of the umbilic points with the elliptical ORT models 1 and 5

steps.action: Derive closed-form umbilic positions, curvature centres, radii and existence conditions on both vertical symmetry planes for the P and two S waves (Tables 3-6).
steps.quote: To ensure the existence of the analytical solutions, specific conditions for model parameters need to be satisfied.

steps.action: Plot the analytical umbilic positions for all seven elliptical models (Figure 3), noting models where the existence conditions fail and no S1 or S2 umbilic exists.
steps.quote: By using the derived analytical expressions, we show positions of the umbilic points for all seven elliptical ORT models

steps.action: Compare ellipsoidal slowness and traveltime with the shifted-hyperbola forms near the umbilic, and map the relative traveltime error for models 1 and 5 (Figures 4-5).
steps.quote: Generally, the difference in traveltime is not very big for all tested cases.

steps.action: For anelliptical ORT models, where no analytical form can be derived, switch to numerical evaluation of the condition in equation (6).
steps.quote: only the numerical test can be implemented to examine the location of umbilic points

steps.action: Set seven anelliptical ORT models built on the elliptical ones by adding delta1-delta3 with different values and signs (Tables 7-8).
steps.quote: [...] seven anelliptical ORT models with the normalized stiffness coefficients shown in Table 7

steps.action: Vary delta_i (models 1-3, Figure 6) and epsilon (models 6-7, Figure 7), then plot all seven models (Figure 8): umbilics shift between planes, multiply, and appear off the symmetry planes.
steps.quote: corresponding tests are made to check the influence on umbilic points from the newly added anisotropy parameters

steps.action: Map traveltime differences for the anelliptical models (Figures 9-11, depth 1 km) and compare them with the elliptical case in Figure 5.
steps.quote: Compared with the plots in Figure 5, we can see that the difference from the S1 wave becomes more significant

steps.action: Attribute the larger deviations at particular umbilic points (S2 and S1 waves, model 7; Figures 12-14) to interference between neighbouring umbilic points.
steps.quote: The deviation is caused by the interference of two nearby umbilic points

steps.action: Restrict the analytical formulas to near offsets or weak anellipticity; state that anelliptical positions can only be found numerically from known parameters.
steps.quote: which can be utilized for ORT models near offsets or weak in anellipticity

steps.action: Keep the derived existence conditions and position expressions, the shifted-hyperbola traveltime procedure, and the interference observation as the paper's conclusions.
steps.quote: We observed that remarkable deviations are caused by the interference of nearby umbilic points.

tree.answer: Umbilic points (equal principal curvatures) on ORT slowness surfaces
No; computed from synthetic models, no data
Locate umbilics and quantify the traveltime deviation they cause
Conditions set in seven elliptical and seven anelliptical synthetic models
Varying delta and epsilon moves umbilics off the symmetry planes; elliptical result holds only for weak anellipticity
Analytical formulas kept for elliptical ORT; numerical-only for anelliptical

end.claim: Umbilic-point existence conditions and explicit position formulas are derived for elliptical ORT media, with a shifted-hyperbola procedure for the traveltime deviation they cause; anelliptical cases need numerical search and show larger deviations from interfering neighbouring umbilics.

decisive_move.sentence: The analytical derivation of umbilic positions, curvature centres and existence conditions for the elliptical ORT model (Tables 3-6) is the core result; without it only numerical contours remain.

gates.evidence: Some synthetic models were chosen to span the signs of gamma1, gamma2 and epsilon1-epsilon2 set by the derived conditions (p. 399), but no hypothesis directed the acquisition of any data. The analytical formulas are not explicitly checked against the numerical contours (Figure 2 vs Tables 3-6), and the interference explanation is not tested. Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: Umbilic points, principal, Gaussian and mean curvatures of a surface (Abbena et al. 2017; Cazals & Pouget 2004)
Centre and radius of curvature of a surface point (Casey 2012)

limits: Purely theoretical and numerical: synthetic models only, no field or lab data. The paper does not state that the analytical positions in Tables 3-6 were checked against the numerically located zeros in Figure 2 (inference: they may agree, but no comparison is reported). The interference explanation (p. 400) is asserted from plots, with no rival and no test. The VTI and HTI statements (p. 400) are given without shown computations. Composition none_fits: the walk is derivation, then synthetic-model exploration, then parameter variation, with no rivals, crucial test, or found conditions. Sub-claims and their status: the elliptical analytical formulas are capability_characterized; the anelliptical off-plane umbilics are a numerical observation in the tested models only; the interference cause is at most a proposed explanation (status none beyond best guess). The acknowledgements mention an editor, an associate editor and three reviewers, but no review file was supplied, so changes made in review cannot be coded. Data and codes are available only on request.

disagreements.support: The authors swap the plane indices for epsilon, delta and gamma relative to Tsvankin's convention, a notation choice with no evidential claim.
disagreements.quote: Notice that the indexation for anisotropy parameters differs from those defined in Tsvankin (1997)
